Because iOS Safari zooms the page into any field under 16px and leaves it zoomed after typing. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | |-|-|-|-|-| | `--font-sans` | every word | every word | code | `"Hanken Grotesk", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif` | | `--font-mono` | code and keys only | code and keys | labels, amounts | `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace` | | `--text-xs` | captions, counters | captions, counters, badges | body | `12px` | | `--text-sm` | controls and body | controls, menu items, dense body | phone fields | `14px` | | `--text-base` | prose, large controls | prose, messages, large button | dense rows | `16px` | | `--text-lg` | a small heading | card and empty state titles | body | `18px` | | `--text-xl` | a section or overlay heading | dialog and section headings | controls | `22px` | | `--text-2xl` | a page heading | a page title | section headings | `28px` | | `--text-3xl` | a display figure | a display figure such as the balance | headings | `36px` | | `--leading-tight` | headings | text-lg and up | prose | `1.2` | | `--leading-snug` | labels and short copy | buttons, cards, short copy | prose | `1.35` | | `--leading-normal` | prose | prose | headings | `1.5` | | `--tracking-tight` | large headings only; Lime never tracks out | text-xl and up | small text | `-0.01em` | | `--weight-normal` | body | body | headings | `400` | | `--weight-medium` | controls and labels | controls and labels | body | `500` | | `--weight-semibold` | headings | headings and titles | long runs | `600` | ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Caption, hint, badge | `--text-xs` | | Button, input, menu item | `--text-sm` | | Message, prose, large button | `--text-base` | | Card, empty state or page section heading | `--text-lg` | | Dialog or sheet title | `title-overlay (--text-xl)` | | Page title | `title-page (--text-xl on a phone, --text-2xl from sm)` | | Control label, list title | `label` | | Body copy in a screen | `body` | | Account balance | `--text-3xl` | ## Scale Sizes 12, 14, 16, 18, 22, 28, 36px. --- name: Anti-slop system: quartz kind: foundation last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/anti-slop --- # Anti-slop The habits of generated UI to avoid, and what to do instead. ## Rules 1. anti-slop-no-caps NEVER Set text in capitals or tracked out; keep sentence case. Because capitals read slower and make every label shout, so a real warning no longer stands out. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `Running` 2. anti-slop-mono-for-copyable MUST Set mono only for code, commands, paths, IDs, keys and hashes; numbers get the data utility. Because mono marks what a person copies, so a mono duration looks like an id. - Correct: `2m 14s` - Wrong: `2m 14s` 3. anti-slop-no-em-dash NEVER Use an em dash for a pause or an empty value; end the sentence, or write None. Because an empty cell with a dash reads as a minus or a value still loading, and a screen reader may skip it. - Correct: `
{run.owner ?? 'None'}
` - Wrong: `
{run.owner ?? '\u2014'}
` 4. anti-slop-no-dot-separator NEVER Join facts with a middle dot; give each its own element with a gap. Because a screen reader reads each dot aloud, and the string wraps mid-fact on a phone. - Correct: `{model}{variant}{time}` - Wrong: `` `${model} · ${variant} · ${time}` `` 5. anti-slop-no-eyebrow NEVER Put a small category label above a title. Because it repeats the sidebar and makes two headings compete for the first read. - Correct: `

Input

` - Wrong: `

Components

Input

` 6. anti-slop-no-side-rail NEVER Mark selection, quotes or panels with a bar on one edge or a stripe across a card; use the wash between frame lines. Because an edge bar reads as a status stripe, so a selected row looks flagged. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `data-selected:shadow-[inset_2px_0_0_var(--accent-mark)]` 7. anti-slop-no-card-grid NEVER Show several numbers as three equal icon cards; compose one stats strip, a table or a sentence. Because equal cards give every number the same weight and push the table the person came for below the fold. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `42 x3` 8. anti-slop-no-pill NEVER Round a label, tag or filter fully; use rounded-inner or rounded-soft. Round is for people, the radio and the switch. Because a pill reads as a toggle, so people click a static tag. - Correct: `Beta` - Wrong: `beta` 9. anti-slop-no-box-in-box NEVER Put a bordered or grey box inside a frame; split it with row rules or a well. Because a box in a box stacks edges until no one can tell which group a line closes. - Wrong: `
…
` 10. anti-slop-no-centred-empty NEVER Centre an empty state in a big box; put it top-left of the body with the query in a code tag. Because a centred block in a void reads as a template and moves the action away from where the first row was. - Wrong: `` 11. anti-slop-no-tinted-alert NEVER Fill an alert with a tinted block; frame it and mark trouble with the status icon and a title that names it. Because a tinted block buries the words under the colour and reads like every Bootstrap alert. - Wrong: `
Sync failed
` 12. anti-slop-no-red-button NEVER Fill a destructive button red; give it the fail edge and fail text. Because a red fill is the loudest shape on the page and outshouts the primary action. - Wrong: `` 13. anti-slop-no-ink-decoration NEVER Fill a header, kind, icon tile or second button with ink; ink fill is the primary button, one per view, and a checked control. Because when headers and tiles are ink too, the primary action no longer stands out. - Wrong: `
Runs
` 14. anti-slop-no-hue-wallpaper NEVER Fill a section, card or header with a kind hue; put the hue in a label, a chart line or the selected row. Because a hue names a kind, so a filled section makes everything inside look like that kind. - Wrong: `
` 15. anti-slop-no-icon-tiles NEVER Put a category icon in a colored tile; write the kind as a tinted word. Because the tile spends the hue on decoration, and the glyph names nothing a screen reader can read. - Wrong: `` 16. anti-slop-no-status-dots NEVER Write status as a dot, square or pill; write the word, and color only warn and fail. Because a dot carries status by hue alone, which color-blind people, forced colors and screen readers all lose. - Wrong: ` api@v312` 17. anti-slop-no-outline-rings NEVER Ring a filled mark or badge in a dark 1px outline; leave the fill flat. Because the ring reads as focus or selection, so people think the badge is active. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 18. anti-slop-no-empty-art NEVER Draw art in an empty state; write a title, one muted line and the action. Because the art pushes the action below the fold on a phone and says nothing about why the list is empty. - Correct: `No agents yetCreate one to start.` - Wrong: `No agents yet` 19. anti-slop-no-decorative-motion NEVER Pulse, ping, bounce, glow or sweep to look alive; a running status is a small turning arc. Because constant motion takes the eye from the row that changed and keeps moving under reduced motion. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 20. anti-slop-no-terminal-cosplay NEVER Use prompt signs, block cursors or bracketed labels outside a terminal; use the normal component. Because a screen reader reads the signs and brackets aloud, and people try to type at the fake cursor. - Correct: `Deployed` - Wrong: `

> [OK] deploy complete_

` 21. anti-slop-no-arrow-links NEVER End link text in an arrow or write Learn more; name where the link goes. Because a screen reader listing links hears ten Learn mores and no destination. - Correct: `Rotating API keys` - Wrong: `Learn more →` 22. anti-slop-no-shimmer-text NEVER Sweep a gradient through in-progress text; keep the text still and show the running status. Because the sweep drops the text under its contrast floor mid-pass and never says when the work stops. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `Thinking` 23. anti-slop-no-glass NEVER Blur or fade an overlay, bar or card; use the solid surface and the overlay shadow. Because the page shows through and pulls the overlay text under its contrast floor. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 24. anti-slop-no-grey-prose NEVER Set a sentence at label-sm in text-3; use body-sm or larger in text-2. Because 12px at the 5:1 floor holds a word or two, and a whole sentence there is tiring to read. - Correct: `

Runs older than 30 days move to cold storage.

` - Wrong: `

Runs older than 30 days move to cold storage.

` 25. anti-slop-no-icon-every-label NEVER Put an icon on every button, menu item or heading; icons are for actions found by shape. Because when every item has a glyph, none can be found by its shape. - Correct: `Rename` - Wrong: `Rename` 26. anti-slop-no-filler NEVER Write seamless, robust, effortless or leverage; name the mechanism or the number. Because the words promise without telling the person what happens or how fast. - Correct: `Deploys an agent in 42 seconds to 3 regions.` - Wrong: `Seamlessly deploy robust agents.` ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Distinguish a kind | `` | | Show a state | ` with its word` | | Separate containers | `one frame line; rows split by rule-row` | | Mark selection | `--accent-wash between frame lines` | ## Reject list - Caps, mono labels, dots between facts, eyebrows. - Side bars, pills, hue fills, icon tiles, status dots, grey slabs, tinted blocks, centred voids. - Glass, glow, shimmer, terminal costume. ## Related - [Color](/systems/quartz/foundations/color.md): Five hues name the kind of thing, and amber and red mean trouble. - [Typography](/systems/quartz/foundations/typography.md): One sans for every word, mono for what a person copies. - [Iconography](/systems/quartz/foundations/iconography.md): A few solid icons, only for actions you find by their shape.

--- name: Borders and lines system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/borders-and-lines --- # Borders and lines One quiet grey line around each Card, a fainter rule between its rows, and a stronger edge on each control; a Panel is the grey widget with a quiet frame line. ## Rules 1. borders-and-lines-card-panel MUST Draw a working surface (a big table or stream, a trace, a log, code, a form, the detail of one object) as a white Card: one grey edge and a rule under its header. Draw a widget or a decision (an overview, a chart widget, a short list, a card that asks Resume or Roll back) as a Panel: grey outer with a quiet frame line, the header on the grey, the content in a white bordered body 4px in, the footer back on the grey. Because a working surface needs its edge and header rule to show where it ends, while a widget reads best as a quiet grey group whose body is the one white group and whose buttons rest on the grey. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 2. borders-and-lines-no-mixed-frames NEVER A widget is a Panel and a working surface is a Card; never a Card inside a Panel or a Panel inside a Card. Because a white card in a grey panel is a box in a box; side by side, the grey widget and the white table tell the person which one to glance at and which one to work in. - Correct: `
…
` - Wrong: `` 3. borders-and-lines-one-frame MUST Give a component one frame line and split its rows with rule-row; never a box in a box. Because a box in a box stacks edges until no one can tell which group a line closes. - Correct: `
…
` - Wrong: `…` 4. borders-and-lines-row-rules MUST Split rows with rule-row, the 8% line; the last row drops it because the frame line is right below. Because a row rule as heavy as the frame line reads as a second box, and a rule on the last row doubles the bottom edge. - Correct: `
  • ` - Wrong: `
  • ` 5. borders-and-lines-control-edge MUST Give every control its 1px control edge at rest; it is ink at 50%, 3.3:1 on paper, and neither --line-frame nor --line-row is ever a control's only edge. Because the frame line and row rule are decorative and fall under 3:1, so a control drawn with them has no edge a person can find until they hover. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 6. borders-and-lines-shared-line MUST Draw cells side by side in a ButtonGroup (frame-shared), so neighbours meet on one line. Because two cells that each draw a full border paint the shared pixel twice, and a translucent line reads heavier where they meet. - Correct: `
    {cells.map(c => )}
    ` - Wrong: `
    {cells.map(c => )}
    ` 7. borders-and-lines-wash-selection MUST Mark selection with the wash and the frame line above and below; never a bar on one edge. Because an edge bar reads as a status stripe, and a wash alone vanishes in forced colors where the lines survive. - Correct: `` 8. borders-and-lines-focus MUST Show focus on a field (input, textarea, select, date trigger, OTP, composer, code editor) by turning its edge ink with a soft 3px ink halo around it (--focus-halo), eased, with no outline. Every other keyboard target, such as a button, gets a 2px ink outline at a 2px offset; in a strip or a list the ring sits inside the cell (focus-ring-inset), and on an ink fill it is paper (focus-ring-ink). Because a field already has an edge, so an outline on top doubles it; an offset ring on a button lands on the neighbour's shared line, and an ink ring on an ink fill is 1:1. - Correct: `focus-visible:focus-ring-inset data-checked:focus-visible:focus-ring-ink` ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as light) | |-|-|-|-|-|-| | `--line-hair` | dividers, rings | separator, ring | | `1px` | | | `--line-accent` | the 2px accent stroke | active tab line, chart stroke | dividers | `2px` | | | `--line-focus` | focus outline width | focus outline width | borders | `2px` | | | `--focus-offset` | focus outline offset | every focusable | | `2px` | | | `--line-frame-alpha` | the ink alpha of a frame's edge: a quiet grey line, so a screen of frames reads light | line-frame | | `0.14` | `0.20` | | `--mark-size` | the legend square and the menu radio dot | chart legend, radio item | | `8px` | | | `--ring-cutout` | the gap ring that cuts an overlapping avatar out of the surface | avatar group | | `2px` | | | `--chart-dash` | stroke-dasharray for a comparison or projected series | chart | | `6 4` | | | `--chart-axis-gap` | gap between a tick label and the plot; chart.tsx reads it into its layout | chart | | `8px` | | | `--border-hair` | a divider where fields cannot separate | old hairline, kept until its last reader goes | anything new | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.08)` | | | `--border-faint` | a divider inside a grey card | card rows | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.05)` | | | `--border-strong` | the strongest hairline | input hover, outline button | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.12)` | | | `--border-control` | the edge of an empty control, 3.4:1 on --surface-page, 3.3:1 on --surface-card (WCAG 1.4.11) | checkbox, radio, switch | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.50)` | | | `--border-focus` | focus outline, always ink | focus outline, always ink | hover | `var(--ink)` | | | `--line-frame` | the one outer edge of a component, 1px, a quiet grey | the one outer edge of a component and of an overlay; --- name: Color system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/color --- # Color Frost: cold navy ink on icy paper, cards on a cool fog canvas. Five cold hues name the kind of thing, and amber and red mean trouble. ## Rules 1. color-hue-is-a-noun MUST Give each kind one hue everywhere: agent, key, run, deploy and model, in that order. Always show the word. Because a person learns cyan as agent once and reads it on every screen, and the word carries the kind in grayscale and aloud. - Correct: `` 2. color-warm-is-trouble NEVER Use amber or red for anything but warn and fail; no kind, chart series or decoration is warm. Because an operator scanning for trouble stops on every warm mark, so a warm Beta tag reads as a failing run. - Correct: `Retrying` - Wrong: `Beta` 3. color-set-kind-attribute MUST Set data-kind or data-status on a panel and read --accent-wash and --accent-line; never name a hue in a component. Because a hard-coded hue skips the dark theme value and keeps its color when the kind changes. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `` 4. color-no-hue-fills NEVER Fill a tile, icon, section, card or header with a hue; hue goes in a kind label, a chart line or the selected row. Because a hue names a kind, so a filled section makes everything inside it look like that kind. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 5. color-ink-text MUST Set text in --text-1 to --text-3 (ink at 100, 80, 66%); --text-disabled is for disabled controls only. A disabled ink fill (the primary Button) has no grey to turn, so the whole key fades to --dim-opacity instead. Because text-3 is the 5:1 floor, and a palette grey like gray-500 falls under it on the grey card and in the dark theme. - Correct: `

` - Wrong: `

` 6. color-ink-fill MUST Fill with ink only the primary Button (one per view) and a control that is checked, such as a checkbox, radio or switch. Mark what waits on a person with the soft label, InkSlot, which is a grey fill with ink text. Because the primary button is the one thing to do next, and an ink header or kind tile takes that place from it. - Correct: `Waiting on you` - Wrong: `

Runs

` 7. color-selection-wash MUST Mark selection with --accent-wash, or the neutral selected fill, and keep the wash on hover. Because a selected row that swaps to the hover fill looks deselected under the pointer. - Correct: `data-selected:bg-accent-wash` 8. color-line-step MUST Draw a 2px line or ring in a hue with the line step, --accent-line. Because the mark step is a fill that falls under 3:1 on paper, and only the line step clears 3:1 for a stroke. - Correct: `className="stroke-accent-line"` - Wrong: `stroke="var(--hue-3-mark)"` 9. color-surface-attr SHOULD Use data-surface (card, raised, overlay, paper, ink, inverse) to name what an element is painted as. Because nested tokens recompute from it, so text and lines inside keep their contrast. - Correct: `

never set or read them in a component. `--hue-1-mark`, `--hue-1-field`, `--hue-1-wash`, `--hue-1-line`, `--hue-1-tint`, `--hue-1-label`, `--hue-2-mark`, `--hue-2-field`, `--hue-2-wash`, `--hue-2-line`, `--hue-2-tint`, `--hue-2-label`, `--hue-3-mark`, `--hue-3-field`, `--hue-3-wash`, `--hue-3-line`, `--hue-3-tint`, `--hue-3-label`, `--hue-4-mark`, `--hue-4-field`, `--hue-4-wash`, `--hue-4-line`, `--hue-4-tint`, `--hue-4-label`, `--hue-5-mark`, `--hue-5-field`, `--hue-5-wash`, `--hue-5-line`, `--hue-5-tint`, `--hue-5-label` ## Button tokens Read only through their classes; never set or read them in a component. `--button-primary`, `--key-primary-body`, `--key-primary-body-hover`, `--key-primary-edge`, `--key-primary-edge-press`, `--key-primary-sheen`, `--key-secondary-body`, `--key-secondary-body-hover`, `--key-secondary-edge`, `--key-secondary-edge-press`, `--key-secondary-sheen`, `--button-primary-hover`, `--button-secondary`, `--button-secondary-hover`, `--button-ghost`, `--button-ghost-hover`, `--surface-disabled`, `--ring-thumb` ## Contrast [The table on the human page](https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/color#contrast). ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Body text | `--text-1` | | Hint or caption | `--text-3` | | Label for a kind | `` | | Selected row | `--accent-wash` | | Chart line for a kind | `--accent-line` | | Trouble word | `--warn-text or --fail-text` | | Grey field | `--surface-card` | ## Scale Kinds in slot order: agent cyan, key orchid, run blue, deploy violet, model mint. All cold: warm hues are kept for trouble. Text on every mark is 5:1 or better, on every field and wash 7.5:1, and every line step is 3:1 on paper and the grey card. ## Reject list - No raw hex, rgb or Tailwind palette colors. - No hue fills, gradients or warm kinds. ## Related - [Typography](/systems/quartz/foundations/typography.md): One sans for every word, mono for what a person copies. - [Borders and lines](/systems/quartz/foundations/borders-and-lines.md): Grey fields keep things apart, and hairlines go only where a field cannot.

--- name: Elevation system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/elevation --- # Elevation Paper cards with one grey frame line on a fog canvas; controls sit a pixel above the page, overlays lift with one short shadow. ## Rules 1. elevation-overlay-shell MUST A dialog or sheet is a grey shell with the overlay shadow holding one white card 4px in, with the title, description, close and body in it; the actions sit on the grey. Because the shadow lifts the overlay, and the grey shell with its one white card tells the person where the content is and where the actions are. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 2. elevation-overlays-only MUST Shadow only overlays: menus, popovers, dialogs, sheets, the command palette, tooltips and toasts. Because a shadow says this floats above the page, and a shadowed card makes the person look for what it covers. - Correct: ` // shadow-overlay` - Wrong: `` 3. elevation-one-shadow MUST Use shadow-overlay for every overlay; never write a shadow value. Its 1px frame line is part of shadow-overlay, so an overlay never adds frame. Because a written value keeps its light-theme strength in the dark theme, and frame inside a scrolling overlay scrolls away with the content. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 4. elevation-no-glass NEVER Blur or fade an overlay; use solid paper. Because the page shows through a translucent surface and pulls the menu text under its contrast floor. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `` 5. elevation-well-not-container NEVER Use the grey field as a container; it is a well for code, output and read-only values inside a frame. Because a grey slab around a heading or a button is the box-in-a-box the frame replaces, and on paper it has no edge. - Correct: `
…
` - Wrong: `

Runs

` 6. elevation-dialog-scrim SHOULD Dim the page behind a dialog with --surface-overlay. Because the scrim tells the person the page is inert until the dialog closes. 7. elevation-no-xs-sm NEVER Use shadow-xs or shadow-sm; both are empty in Quartz. Because they draw nothing, so a model that reaches for them to lift a card ships a flat card and thinks it is raised. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as light) | |-|-|-|-|-|-| | `--ink` | solid ink | primary text, primary button | | `oklch(var(--ink-c))` | | | `--paper` | solid paper | page background | | `oklch(var(--paper-c))` | | | `--surface-canvas` | the cool fog an app sits on, behind its cards and frames | app background, docs preview | | `oklch(var(--canvas-c))` | | | `--surface-page` | paper: the ground of every card, frame and panel | card, table, dialog | | `var(--paper)` | | | `--surface-card` | the well: the grey field inside a frame for code, logs, shell output and read-only values; never a container | code, output and read-only values inside a frame | containers | `oklch(var(--grey-c))` | | | `--surface-frame` | a panel's outer frame: lighter than the well, so a page of panels stays bright | panel, overlay shell | | `color-mix(in oklch, var(--surface-card) 55%, var(--paper))` | | | `--surface-raised` | a container inside a grey card | paper; a container inside a grey card | Quartz overlays, which use paper | `var(--paper)` | | | `--surface-hover` | row and item hover | row, menu item, ghost button | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.05)` | | | `--surface-selected` | selected row with no kind, one step past hover | table, data table, tree | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.09)` | | | `--surface-pressed` | active press | row, ghost button | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.08)` | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.28)` | | `--surface-inverse` | a pressed chip or highlighted item on the page's own channels; whole panels use data-surface="inverse" | chip, segmented control | | `var(--ink)` | | | `--surface-tile` | a media square behind an image or file icon, ink at 8% | attachment media | | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.08)` | | | `--surface-overlay` | dialog backdrop | dialog and sheet backdrop | popovers | `oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.24)` | | | `--surface-thumb` | the selected segment: paper on the grey track in light, paper mixed with ink in dark so it reads lighter than the track | segmented control | | `color-mix(in oklch, var(--paper), oklch(var(--ink-c)) var(--thumb-lift))` | | | `--focus-halo` | a field with the cursor: a soft ink halo around its ink edge, eased in | input, select, combobox, date picker, OTP, code editor, composer | | `0 0 0 3px oklch(var(--ink-c) / 0.08)` | | | `--elev-control` | the lift under a paper control, so a button or field sits on the page instead of being drawn on it | a one-pixel drop under a paper control, so a secondary button, field or select sits on the page | cards, rows | `0 1px 2px -1px oklch(var(--text-on-field-c) / calc(var(--shadow-alpha) * 0.6))` | | | `--elev-none` | no lift, for a control that sits flat: disabled and read-only fields | field, select, checkbox, radio, switch, otp | | `0 0 0 0 transparent` | | | `--elev-thumb` | the selected segment lifted off its grey track; in dark a 1px ring joins the shadow | a small shadow, plus a faint ring in the dark theme, that lifts the selected segment off its grey track | cards and overlays | `0 0 0 1px oklch(var(--ink-c) / var(--thumb-ring-alpha)), 0 1px 2px oklch(var(--text-on-field-c) / calc(var(--shadow-alpha) * 0.5))` | | | `--elev-overlay` | the overlay's edge plus one short shadow | 1px frame line plus one short shadow: menu, popover, dialog, sheet, tooltip, toast | cards | `0 0 0 1px var(--line-frame), 0 12px 24px -12px oklch(var(--text-on-field-c) / var(--shadow-alpha))` | | | `--shadow-alpha` | overlay shadow strength; the dark theme raises it | overlay shadow, raised in the dark theme | components | `0.20` | `0.6` | ## Ink and paper tokens Read only through their classes; never set or read them in a component. `--ink-c`, `--paper-c`, `--grey-c`, `--canvas-c`, `--text-on-field-c`, `--shadow-alpha` ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Card, panel, table | `the frame line, no shadow` | | Code or output inside a frame | `well (--surface-card)` | | Menu, popover, tooltip, toast | `--elev-overlay` | | Dialog or sheet | `--elev-overlay and --surface-overlay behind` | ## Scale Three levels: flow (a frame on paper), well (grey inside a frame, no line), overlay (frame line and one shadow). The segmented control's thumb is the one smaller lift, --elev-thumb. ## Reject list - No colored shadows, gradients or backdrop blur. - No grey slab as a container. ## Related - [Borders and lines](/systems/quartz/foundations/borders-and-lines.md): Grey fields keep things apart, and hairlines go only where a field cannot. - [Color](/systems/quartz/foundations/color.md): Five hues name the kind of thing, and amber and red mean trouble.

Because a raw width drifts from the shell, so the page edge no longer lines up with the header and nav. - Correct: `

quartz/iconography.content: --- name: Iconography system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/iconography --- # Iconography A few solid icons from Font Awesome Free, only for actions you find by their shape. ## Rules 1. iconography-actions-only MUST Use an icon only for an action found by its shape: copy, close, search, more, external, chevron, add. Because icons on every row and item stop being findable by shape, and a rocket says nothing a screen reader or a new user can read. - Correct: ```tsx prompt-v13 Rename ``` - Wrong: ```tsx prompt-v13 Rename ``` 2. iconography-import MUST Import icons only through registry/quartz/icon.tsx and draw them with . Because the set is swapped in that one file, and Icon hides the glyph from a screen reader unless it gets a label. - Correct: `import {Icon, Copy} from '@/registry/quartz/icon'` 3. iconography-size MUST Use 16px in controls, rows and icon-only buttons, 12px for a caret or a check inside a control, and 20px or 24px only for a rare large target (a broken image, a drop zone); never pass a weight or stroke. Because the set is Font Awesome Classic Solid, one weight, and these sizes keep glyphs on whole pixels; a stroke prop would outline a filled glyph. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 4. iconography-icon-only-name MUST Give every icon-only button an aria-label. Because the glyph is aria-hidden, so a screen reader announces only "button". - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 5. iconography-no-kind-icons NEVER Draw a kind glyph or put an icon in a colored tile; a kind is a tinted word. Because a glyph has to be learned and a screen reader skips it, where the word names the kind for everyone. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 6. iconography-no-hue NEVER Color an icon; icons are ink. Because a tinted glyph reads as a kind or a status the row does not have, and a glyph in a mark step falls under 3:1 on paper. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | |-|-|-|-|-| | `--control-sm` | small control height, the sm of every control | small icon button box | glyph size | `28px` | | `--control` | default control height, wider than tall: 16px of padding a side | default icon button box | glyph size | `32px` | | `--control-lg` | large control and touch target | large icon button and touch target | glyph size | `44px` | | `--text-1` | primary text, and the only text on marks and fields | icon color | hue | `var(--ink)` | ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Icon in a control | `size 16` | | Icon-only button glyph | `size 16 in every icon-only size (icon-xs to icon-lg); a labelled xs button draws its icon at 14px` | | Caret or check inside a control | `size 12` | | Kind of a thing | `, never a glyph` | | Name of a row or menu item | `the word, no icon` | ## Scale Glyph sizes 12, 16, 20, 24px; 16 almost everywhere, 12 for carets and checks, 20 and 24 for large targets. One set, Font Awesome Classic Solid, one weight. ## Reject list - No kind icons. - No icon before every label. - No hue on icons. ## Related - [Color](/systems/quartz/foundations/color.md): Five hues name the kind of thing, and amber and red mean trouble. - [Anti-slop](/systems/quartz/foundations/anti-slop.md): The habits of generated UI to avoid, and what to do instead.

quartz/motion.content: --- name: Motion system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/motion --- # Motion State changes answer in 60 to 180ms on one standard ease. ## Rules 1. motion-quartzs-snap MUST Change a quartz with a cut or a short ease on --ease-step (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)); nothing glides. Because a status that fades from running to failed shows a half state an operator can misread, and a slow ease makes the change look late. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 2. motion-declare-transitions MUST Give every interactive element a transition: color, background and outline over --dur-fast. Because transition: all also tweens width and padding, which shifts layout on hover, and an element with none cuts while its neighbour tweens. - Correct: `transition: color var(--dur-fast), background-color var(--dur-fast)` - Wrong: `transition: all` 3. motion-hue-cuts NEVER Ease a hue change; border and wash changes may ease. Because mid-tween the color passes through other kinds, so cyan easing to orchid shows the run blue for a moment. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 4. motion-one-thing NEVER Animate for its own sake: no parallax or looping decoration. The running arc and an indeterminate bar are the only loops. Because motion pulls the eye, and a looping decoration takes it from the one row that changed. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `Live` 5. motion-running-arc MUST Show running work as the 3/4 arc before the word, turning smoothly once per --dur-spin. Because the arc stops but stays under reduced motion and pauses offscreen, which a hand-made spinner does not. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `... Running` 6. motion-no-grow NEVER Grow or scale an overlay in; it appears. Because a grow pulls the eye to the motion instead of the content and makes a fast menu feel slow. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 7. motion-collapse-cuts MUST Open and close a panel with a cut; never tween its height. Because a height tween reflows everything below it for 200ms, and the content arrives after the person already looked. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 8. motion-reduced MUST Honour prefers-reduced-motion: base and slow durations and the sheet shift go to zero, loops stop; hover colour stays. Because sliding sheets and loops can make people with vestibular disorders sick, while a 60ms press still tells them the click landed. - Correct: `motion-safe:animate-run` 9. motion-pause-offscreen SHOULD Pause any loop while it is offscreen. Because a loop nobody can see still costs frames and battery. ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as light) | |-|-|-|-|-|-| | `--dur-press` | press feedback | press feedback | hover | `60ms` | | | `--dur-fast` | hover: color, wash and edge changes on every interactive element, and a menu, popover or tooltip leaving, on --ease-step | hover color, wash and edge changes, and an overlay leaving | dialogs | `120ms` | | | `--dur-base` | menus, popovers, selects, tooltips and toasts in, opacity only; --- name: Radius system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/radius --- # Radius Three corners by role, and round means a person. ## Rules 1. radius-roles MUST Pick the corner by what the box is: rounded-frame (10px) for a component's outer edge and every overlay, rounded-soft (6px) for a control, rounded-inner (4px) for a box inside a control or a row. Components already carry theirs, and the frame utility sets the frame corner, so a rounded-* class beside it only fights it. Because the corner says how a box nests, so a button reads as sitting inside a card and a selected segment as sitting inside its track. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 2. radius-nesting MUST Round a box inside another by the outer radius minus the padding between them, and never below 0. A 6px track with 2px of padding holds a 4px thumb. Because when the inner corner is as big as the outer one, the gap between them is wider at the corner than on the sides. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 3. radius-frame-var SHOULD To change the corner of a frame, set --frame-radius on it; the frame utility reads it and falls back to --radius-frame. Because a frame draws its edge and its clip from one radius, and an override on only one of them leaves a gap or a cut-off corner. - Correct: `
` 4. radius-person MUST Use the full radius only for a person (an avatar, the presence mark) and for the two controls whose shape is round: the radio and the switch, track and thumb. Because round is how a person is told apart from an agent or a source at a glance, so a round tag spends that meaning. - Correct: ` ` - Wrong: `` 5. radius-no-pill NEVER Round a label, tag or filter fully. Because a pill reads as a toggle, so people click a static tag, and a round box next to the radio reads as one more option. - Correct: `Beta` - Wrong: `beta` 6. radius-shared-straight MUST In a ButtonGroup or any frame-shared strip, round only the outer corners; the edges cells share stay straight. Because a corner on a shared edge leaves a notch in the one line two cells draw together. - Correct: `…` - Wrong: `
{cells.map(c => )}

Full for a person. Chips are rounded-soft; kbd and small badge variants are rounded-inner. Tailwind's rounded-xs and rounded-sm map to 4px, rounded-md to 6px, rounded-lg and rounded-xl to 10px, but write the role name. ## Reject list - No pills. - No corner outside the three roles. - No rounded corner on a shared edge. - No inner box with the same radius as its outer box. ## Related - [Borders and lines](/systems/quartz/foundations/borders-and-lines.md): Grey fields keep things apart, and hairlines go only where a field cannot. - [Space](/systems/quartz/foundations/space.md): How much room goes between things, in steps of 4px.

--- name: Space system: quartz kind: foundation source: registry/quartz/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/space --- # Space How much room goes between things, in steps of 4px. ## Rules 1. space-scale-only MUST Space with the scale (p-4 is 16px); 2px is for optical nudges only. Because an off-scale gap like 13px breaks the rhythm, so edges that should line up across a panel miss by a pixel or two. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 2. space-control SHOULD Inside a control use 8px between icon and label and 12 to 16px padding. 3. space-card SHOULD Pad a card 16px, with 12px between rows of fields. 4. space-inset MUST Inset card text 16px (px-4). A control, chip or label at a card, header or footer edge sits as far from the edge as from the row's top and bottom: (row height minus control height) / 2. Because a 24px chip in a 40px header and a 28px button in a 44px footer both sit 8px from every edge, so the corners of a stack of cards line up. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 5. space-rows MUST Make a single-line row 40px and a row with a title and a description 56px; a card header is 40px; stacked cards are 12px apart. Because rows of one height scan as a column, and a row that grows by its content makes the lists beside it look misaligned. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 6. space-sections SHOULD Put 32px between app sections and 80px between marketing sections, with 120px above the hero. 7. space-before-lines MUST Try more space or a field before adding a divider line between blocks. Because every extra line competes with the table hairlines and focus rings that carry meaning. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `

--- name: Anti-slop system: sodium kind: foundation last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/anti-slop --- # Anti-slop The habits of generated UI to avoid, and what to do instead. ## Rules 1. anti-slop-no-cell-grid NEVER Draw a cell grid or a dot field behind the page or behind content. Because the owner ruled it out: a grid behind every word fights the rules that carry the layout, and it is the first thing a generated "technical" screen reaches for. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 2. anti-slop-no-terminal-costume NEVER Dress a screen as a terminal: green or amber on black, scanlines, a > prompt before a headline, ASCII boxes. Because Sodium takes the discipline of a terminal, not its look, and a costume makes a real tool read as a toy. - Correct: `

Pipelines

` - Wrong: `

> pipelines_

` 3. anti-slop-no-decoration NEVER Add a gradient, a blob, a glow or a backdrop blur; the one gradient is the light from below that the slab and edged recipes draw on a button. Because Sodium is flat fills and 1px rules, and decoration competes with the one yellow action. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 4. anti-slop-no-rounding NEVER Round a corner to soften a region, a control or an avatar. Because every corner is square, and one round corner is the part everyone sees. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 5. anti-slop-no-yellow-everywhere NEVER Spread yellow past the one primary, the selection and a chart series: no yellow headers, header squares, borders, icons or badges. Because yellow marks the thing to act on, and yellow everywhere marks nothing. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 6. anti-slop-no-stat-cards NEVER Lay out a row of equal cards each holding one number. Because equal boxes make every number equally loud; a status strip puts them on one ruled row where they can be compared. - Correct: `
{cells.map(c =>
…
)}
` - Wrong: `
…
…
` 7. anti-slop-no-box-in-box NEVER Box a part inside a frame; divide it with a rule. Because two edges a few px apart read as a double line. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 8. anti-slop-no-side-rail NEVER Mark a row with a coloured bar on one edge. Because the bar reads as a status nobody defined; a chosen row takes the selection wash, and a row draws nothing at its start. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 9. anti-slop-no-status-dots NEVER Mark a status with a round dot; a status is a square mark and a word. Because a round dot is the one curve on a square screen, and its meaning rides on hue alone. - Correct: `Passed` - Wrong: ` Passed` 10. anti-slop-no-label-above-title NEVER Put a small label, a category or a number above a headline. Because the headline already names the section; a name belongs in a panel header row, never stacked over a title. - Correct: `
Runs
` - Wrong: `

Overview

Runs

` 11. anti-slop-no-caps-sentences NEVER Set a sentence, a description or a headline in mono capitals. Because mono capitals are for words a person scans, and a sentence in them reads slowly and shouts. - Correct: `

The backfill wrote 1,204 partitions.

` - Wrong: `

The backfill wrote 1,204 partitions.

` 12. anti-slop-no-emoji NEVER Use emoji in copy, titles or buttons, or as icons. Because emoji render differently on every device and turn a tool into a chat thread. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 13. anti-slop-no-hype NEVER Write seamless, effortless, supercharge, unleash or blazing; say what happens. Because people trust a tool that states the fact. - Correct: `Each job retries twice before it fails.` - Wrong: `Blazing-fast pipelines.` 14. anti-slop-no-brackets-everywhere SHOULD Keep brackets for a machine action, a tool call or a step an agent took; never around a person's button. Because the bracket says a machine did this, and on a person's action it blurs who acted. 15. anti-slop-no-fake-data SHOULD Fill examples with believable data; never Lorem ipsum, John Doe or 1,234. Because placeholder data hides the truncation and alignment problems real data shows. - Correct: `title="Maya Chen"` - Wrong: `title="John Doe"` 16. anti-slop-no-blinking-caret NEVER Leave a caret blinking at rest, or type text a person is waiting to read. Because the caret belongs to typing; at rest it reads as a field waiting for input, and slow typing hides an answer behind an effect. - Correct: `{typing && }` - Wrong: `` 17. anti-slop-no-scroll-reveal NEVER Fade or slide content in as it scrolls into view. Because content that hides until scrolled is missed. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `` 18. anti-slop-dialog-controlled MUST Open a Dialog with open and onOpenChange; never mount it only while open. Because a dialog that unmounts skips its exit and loses the trigger it returns focus to. - Correct: `...` - Wrong: `{open && ...}` ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | Make something stand out | `the one yellow primary, or the selection wash` | | Show several numbers | `a status strip: one ruled row of cells` | | Fill an empty gutter | `dots, 20px or wider, at most one or two per view` | ## Reject list - Cell grids, terminal costume, gradients, blur, rounding, yellow sprawl, stat card rows, boxes in boxes. - Labels above titles, sentences in capitals, emoji, hype. - A caret blinking at rest, scroll reveals. ## Related - [Color](/systems/sodium/foundations/color.md): White and warm near-black, rules for structure, and one sodium yellow that changes how it shows by theme. - [Typography](/systems/sodium/foundations/typography.md): Mono capitals for the interface, Inter Display for headlines and prose, one weight. - [Borders and lines](/systems/sodium/foundations/borders-and-lines.md): Rules divide content; a frame is a region's one outer edge.

--- name: Borders and lines system: sodium kind: foundation source: registry/sodium/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/borders-and-lines --- # Borders and lines Rules divide content; a frame is a region's one outer edge. ## Rules 1. borders-and-lines-rules-divide MUST Divide the parts of a region with rules (rule-row between rows, rule-col between columns, panel-head over a header row); box only the region itself, with frame. Because a rule says where one part ends without adding an edge of its own, so a dense screen stays one surface instead of a stack of boxes. - Correct: `
…
…
` - Wrong: `
…
…
` 2. borders-and-lines-one-header MUST Open every top-level region with the one header as its frame's first row: panel-head, --head (38px) on the panel fill, the thing's name as written (FrameTitle), then its state, meta and actions at the end (FrameStatus, FrameValue meta, FrameActions), with no kind word before the name. Start the body with the data, never a repeat of the name or the state; Table, LogViewer and CodeWindow draw the same header. Because a product names a thing and then says how it is, so the reader finds which region this is and its state in the same place on every screen, while a KIND prefix in capitals reads like a spec sheet, and a status and headline repeated in the body push the data down. - Correct: ```tsx orders-daily Job failed 02:14 UTC … ``` - Wrong: ```tsx On call orders-daily Job failed

Orders stopped

… ``` 3. borders-and-lines-header-actions MUST Put a header's actions at its end in panel-head-actions, as 26px ghost icon buttons (icon-sm) named with aria-label, 8px apart, the last glyph on the 12px inset (--inset), in one order: search, refresh, wrap, then navigation such as next failure, then the run action, then copy last. Never the yellow slab in a header, and a count belongs in the meta, not on a button. Because the same action sits in the same place in every header, so a hand that copied from the log finds copy in the code window too; the header is the thing's name, so a slab there outshouts it, and a count said twice reads as two different numbers. - Correct: ```tsx ``` - Wrong: ```tsx ``` 4. borders-and-lines-no-page-grid NEVER Draw a grid, a dot field or any pattern behind the page or behind content; structure is rules between content, and dots fill only an empty gutter. Because a cell grid behind every word competes with the rules that carry the layout, and the owner ruled it out. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 5. borders-and-lines-one-weight MUST Draw every line 1px; the focus ring is the only 2px line, and a focused field doubles its own edge inward. Because a 2px rule reads as a selected or focused state. - Correct: `
` - Wrong: `
` 6. borders-and-lines-by-role MUST Pick the line by its job: line-faint between rows; line for a region's edge, a column rule, and the edge of a field, a boxed control, a secondary button and an overlay; line-control only for a small mark: a checkbox, a radio, a switch, a meter track. Because a field or a menu is found by its label, placeholder and fill, so it takes the rule a card draws and every bordered thing reads as one family, while a 16px box in line, 1.3:1 on white, disappears. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 7. borders-and-lines-dots-sparingly SHOULD Use dots only in a gutter 20px or wider with nothing in it, at most one or two per view. Because the texture is decoration; past a couple of gutters it turns into the grid Sodium does not draw. ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as light) | |-|-|-|-|-|-| | `--line-faint` | the rule between rows inside a region | between rows inside a region | edges | `#efede6` | `#22211e` | | `--line` | the rule that divides content and the edge of a field, a boxed control and an overlay, 1.3:1 on the page | a region's edge, a column rule, a header's underline, a field, a segmented control, a secondary button, an overlay | checkbox, radio, switch | `#e2dfd5` | `#2c2a25` | | `--line-control` | the edge of a small mark that would vanish on white, 3.7:1 on the page and 3.3:1 on the well (WCAG 1.4.11) | a checkbox, radio or switch edge, a meter track, a chart cursor, a swimlane connector | fields, overlays, rules between rows | `#8a8478` | `#736d61` | | `--mark` | the rail's dots and a tool-call stack's dashed connectors | rail dots, a tool-call stack's connectors | text | `#8a8478` | `#736d61` | | `--dot` | the dots of a dot-matrix gutter, decoration only | a dot gutter | behind content | `#dedad0` | `#2a2824` | | `--line-width` | every line: rules, edges, connectors | frame, field, rule, overlay | | `1px` | | | `--focus-width` | the focus ring | every focusable | | `2px` | | | `--focus-offset` | the gap between a control and its ring | every focusable | | `2px` | | | `--dot-pitch` | the spacing of a dot-matrix gutter | dots | | `4px` | | | `--rail-pitch` | the spacing of a rail's square dots | rail | | `6px` | | | `--rail-dot` | one rail dot, square | rail | | `2px` | | | `--pending-cell` | one square of the pending mark; four of them, 2px apart | button pending, switch pending, search pending | | `3px` | | ## Decision table | You need | Use | |-|-| | A region: a table, a log, a pipeline's page | `frame` | | Between rows | `rule-row` | | Between columns | `rule-col, no gap` | | A region's header | `panel-head, --head (38px), 12px sides: name as written, then state, meta, actions` | | A header's actions | `26px ghost icons, 8px apart: search, refresh, wrap, navigation, run, copy last` | | A raised region on its own | `panel` | | A gap that must be there | `dots, 20px or wider, nothing in it` | | The start of a quote in a response | `rail; a row never draws one` | ## Scale Every line is 1px. Rules in line-faint and line; fields, boxed controls and overlays in line too; small marks in line-control. ## Reject list - No cell grid or dot field behind the page or content. - No box in a box: rules inside a frame. - No 2px rules, no coloured side bars. ## Related - [Space](/systems/sodium/foundations/space.md): A 4px grid, 32px controls and 40px rows. - [Elevation](/systems/sodium/foundations/elevation.md): No shadows: an overlay is the panel with a rule edge, set apart by its fill and, for a dialog, the scrim.

--- name: Color system: sodium kind: foundation source: registry/sodium/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/color --- # Color White and warm near-black, rules for structure, and one sodium yellow that changes how it shows by theme. ## Rules 1. color-roles-only MUST Read a role such as text-text-2, bg-panel or border-line; never write a hex, an rgb() or a dark: variant. Because the dark theme swaps every role's value, and a typed colour or a dark: pair stays behind. - Correct: `

` - Wrong: `

` 2. color-yellow-rules NEVER Set text, an icon or a lone line in solid yellow (accent-fill); yellow-family text is text-accent-text, and a yellow fill always sits under ink. Because sodium yellow on white is 1.4:1, so a yellow word or icon disappears in the light theme, which is the default. - Correct: `Running` - Wrong: `Running` 3. color-one-slab MUST Keep solid yellow to the one primary button in a view, a chart series and a value chosen inside a small control (the checked recipe); a place you are takes the selected wash, not the slab. Because the slab is how a person finds the next action, and a second slab on the screen splits that in two; a checked box, radio, switch or segment takes yellow as a state, not an action, and it is small and carries an ink mark, so it does not compete with the slab. - Correct: `

Current job
` - Wrong: `
Current job
` 4. color-warn-orange MUST Show a warning in orange (warn, warn-text, warn-tint) with its word, never in yellow. Because yellow is the brand and already means "act here", so a yellow warning reads as the primary action. - Correct: `Over budget` - Wrong: `Over budget` 5. color-status-word MUST Pair a status colour with its word, such as Failed or Passed, never colour alone. Because green, orange and red alone fail people with colour blindness, in grayscale and in forced colours. - Correct: `Failed` - Wrong: `` 6. color-text-tiers SHOULD Use text-1 for values and labels, text-2 for descriptions, text-3 for axes, placeholders and column heads at rest; all three read at 4.5:1 or more. Because the tiers are a hierarchy of attention, not of legibility, so a dense table stays readable down to its axis ticks. ## Tokens | Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as ---
name: Elevation
system: sodium
kind: foundation
source: registry/sodium/tokens.css
last-updated: 2026-10-26
human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/elevation
---

# Elevation

No shadows: an overlay is the panel with a rule edge, set apart by its fill and, for a dialog, the scrim.

## Rules
1. elevation-no-shadows NEVER Cast a shadow: no shadow-*, drop-shadow-* or box-shadow, on regions, buttons or overlays. The one box-shadow is the 1px halo the slab and edged recipes draw under the pointer: a ring flush with the edge, no blur, no offset. Because Sodium is drawn in 1px rules on flat fills, so a blur is the one soft edge on the screen, and every shadow class draws nothing here; a button reads as pressable by light from below inside its face and a hairline halo on hover (the slab and edged recipes), never by a shadow under it.
   - Correct: `<div className="overlay">`
   - Wrong: `<div className="overlay shadow-lg">`
2. elevation-overlay-edge MUST Draw a menu, popover or dialog with the overlay recipe: the panel fill and a 1px line edge, the rule a card draws. Because every bordered thing in Sodium shares one edge colour, so the overlay reads as one more ruled region, set apart by its panel fill and its place over the content.
   - Correct: `<div className="overlay">`
   - Wrong: `<div className="bg-page border border-line-control">`
3. elevation-scrim MUST Dim the page behind a dialog with --scrim: ink at 32% in light, black at 64% in dark. Because the dim says the page is inert until the dialog closes, and a near-black page needs the fixed dark to dim at all.
   - Correct: `<div className="fixed inset-0 bg-scrim"/>`
4. elevation-layers-under-docs MUST Keep a specimen's overlays on --z-overlay (50) and never higher, so the docs' own floating bar stays on top. Because an overlay opened in a preview that climbs past the docs bar covers the theme switch and the install button.
   - Correct: `className="z-(--z-overlay)"`
   - Wrong: `className="z-[100]"`

## Tokens
| Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light | Dark (blank: same as light) |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--shadow-none` | the only shadow Sodium has: nothing casts one, overlays included; the buttons' 1px halo is a ring, not a shadow | the only shadow value | anything that lifts | `none` |  |
| `--z-raised` | a part lifted over its siblings inside a component | sticky header, focused cell |  | `10` |  |
| `--z-overlay` | every portalled layer, under the docs' own floating layers; the last opened sits on top | dialog, popover, menu, tooltip, toast |  | `50` |  |
| `--overlay-sm` | a small dialog | alert dialog |  | `400px` |  |
| `--overlay` | the default dialog and sheet width | dialog, sheet |  | `480px` |  |
| `--overlay-lg` | a wide dialog: a preview, the command palette | dialog lg, command |  | `640px` |  |
| `--popover` | a popover's width | popover |  | `288px` |  |
| `--toast` | a toast's width on a wide screen | toast |  | `360px` |  |
| `--menu-min` | the narrowest a menu opens | dropdown menu, select |  | `192px` |  |
| `--popup-max` | the tallest a list popup grows before it scrolls | select, combobox, menu |  | `320px` |  |
| `--tooltip-max` | a tooltip's line length before it wraps | tooltip |  | `256px` |  |
| `--label-col` | the widest a label column grows before its labels wrap | data list, key and value block |  | `160px` |  |
| `--meter` | the thickness of a meter or progress track | meter, progress |  | `8px` |  |
| `--measure` | a paragraph's longest line | prose, lead |  | `68ch` |  |
| `--measure-hint` | a description or hint's longest line | field hint, row description |  | `60ch` |  |
| `--scrim` | the dim behind a dialog: ink at 32% | behind a dialog or sheet | popovers | `rgb(22 21 18 / 0.32)` | `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.64)` |
| `--line` | the rule that divides content and the edge of a field, a boxed control and an overlay, 1.3:1 on the page | the overlay's edge, the same rule a card draws | checkbox, radio, switch | `#e2dfd5` | `#2c2a25` |
| `--panel` | a raised region, a hair warmer than the page, read by its rules more than its fill | the overlay's fill | the page | `#fafaf7` | `#1c1b19` |

## Decision table
| You need | Use |
|-|-|
| A region on the page | `frame, no lift` |
| A menu or popover | `overlay` |
| A dialog | `overlay over --scrim` |

## Scale
Levels: the page, a frame on it, an overlay (panel and a rule edge), a dialog (an overlay over the scrim). Nothing casts a shadow. The primary and secondary buttons are lit from below inside their own face and take a 1px halo on hover; they lighten and never lift.

## Reject list
- No shadows of any kind, overlays included; the buttons' 1px halo is a ring, not a shadow.
- No backdrop blur.

## Related
- [Color](/systems/sodium/foundations/color.md): White and warm near-black, rules for structure, and one sodium yellow that changes how it shows by theme.
- [Borders and lines](/systems/sodium/foundations/borders-and-lines.md): Rules divide content; a frame is a region's one outer edge.

---
name: Iconography
system: sodium
kind: foundation
source: registry/sodium/tokens.css
last-updated: 2026-10-26
human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/iconography
---

# Iconography

Lucide at 16px, squared off to match square corners.

## Rules
1. iconography-one-source MUST Import icons from Sodium's icon file and draw them with Icon, never from lucide-react or another set. Because the icon file squares each glyph's line ends and joins and holds its line at 1.25px, and Icon sets the size from Sodium's scale and hides a decorative glyph from screen readers; a glyph straight from the package does none of it.
   - Correct: `import {Icon, Add} from '@/components/sodium/icon'`
   - Wrong: `import {Plus} from 'lucide-react'`
2. iconography-sizes MUST Size an icon 16px in every control and row, 14px (--icon-sm) only inside a small field or filter cell, 20px on its own, 24 or 32px only over an empty state. Because the line is 1.25px at every size, so a glyph under 14 crowds and one at 40 looks thin; a small field's 12 or 13px text is shorter than a 16px glyph, which hangs below it, so the field takes the one step down; fixed steps keep icons in a row the same size.
   - Correct: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Add"><Icon icon={Add}/></Button>  // 16px`
   - Wrong: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Add"><Icon icon={Add} size={14}/></Button>`
3. iconography-name-icon-only MUST Name every icon-only control with aria-label; an icon on its own is decorative. Because Icon is aria-hidden unless it has a label, so an icon button with no name is announced as "button".
   - Correct: `<Button size="icon" aria-label="Copy job ID"><Icon icon={Copy}/></Button>`
   - Wrong: `<Button size="icon"><Icon icon={Copy}/></Button>`
4. iconography-colour NEVER Draw an icon in solid yellow on a light ground; an icon takes its label's colour. Because a yellow glyph on white is 1.4:1 and vanishes, and an icon in its own colour reads as a status.
   - Correct: `<Icon icon={Lightning} className="text-text-2"/>`
   - Wrong: `<Icon icon={Lightning} className="text-accent-fill"/>`
5. iconography-no-word MUST Draw an icon only where there is no word: an icon-only button named with aria-label (a region header's actions are these), inside an input (search), or a status glyph. A labeled button carries no icon; a menu trigger's caret is the control's own mark, as on a select. Because the mono capital label already says what the button does, so a glyph beside it says it twice, and once some labeled buttons carry one and others do not, a row reads as two kinds of button.
   - Correct:
     ```tsx
     <Button>Run pipeline</Button>
     <Button size="icon" aria-label="Replay run"><Icon icon={Renew}/></Button>
     ```
   - Wrong: `<Button><Icon icon={Play}/>Run pipeline</Button>`

## Tokens
| Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--icon` | an icon in a control: the set is drawn at 16 | every control and row | empty states | `16px` |
| `--icon-sm` | an icon inside a small field beside its 12 or 13px text, so the glyph spans the caps, not a line and a half | inside a small field or filter cell, beside 12 or 13px text | buttons | `14px` |

## Decision table
| You need | Use |
|-|-|
| A button with a label | `the label alone, no icon` |
| An icon in a row, an input or an icon-only button | `<Icon icon={...}/>, 16px` |
| An icon in a small (26px) field or filter cell | `nothing: the field draws its slots at --icon-sm, 14px` |
| An icon-only button | `Button size="icon" with aria-label` |
| The glyph over an empty state | `24 or 32px in text-3` |
| A glyph the set lacks | `import it from lucide-react in icon.tsx, wrap it with squared and name it there` |

## Scale
16px in UI, 14 inside a small field, 20 on its own, 24 and 32 over an empty state. One weight; the line is 1.25px at every size, with square ends and mitred joins.

## Reject list
- No second icon set, no round line ends, no duotone or filled glyphs, no emoji as icons, no yellow glyph on a light ground.

## Related
- [Typography](/systems/sodium/foundations/typography.md): Mono capitals for the interface, Inter Display for headlines and prose, one weight.

sodium/motion.content:
---
name: Motion
system: sodium
kind: foundation
source: registry/sodium/tokens.css
last-updated: 2026-10-26
human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/motion
---

# Motion

Typing, scrambles, wipes and connectors that draw; ease-out, no springs.

## Rules
1. motion-mechanical MUST Move things the way a machine would: a cut for a state flip, a linear wipe along a rule, typing for text, ease-out only for a move across the screen. The one soft change is a button lighting under the pointer. Because Sodium reads as instruments, and a soft fade or a drift on a status change hides the moment it changed.
   - Correct: `className="wipe"`
   - Wrong: `className="transition-opacity duration-700"  // a failed run fading in`
2. motion-no-springs NEVER Use a spring, a bounce, an overshoot or a press scale; every move eases out and stops. Because an overshoot reads as a toy in an ops tool and delays the moment the thing settles.
   - Correct: `transition-timing-function: var(--ease-out)`
   - Wrong: `transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`
3. motion-type-once MUST Type or scramble a label once, when it first appears or its value changes, and never on a value a person is reading or editing. Because a value that keeps moving cannot be read or copied, and a scramble on every render is noise.
   - Correct: `<Scramble text={label} trigger="mount"/>`
   - Wrong: `<Scramble text={rows} loop/>`
4. motion-caret-while-typing NEVER Leave a caret blinking at rest; it shows only while text types and goes when the text is done. Because a blinking caret pulls the eye after the words are there, and it reads as a field waiting for input.
   - Correct: `{typing && <span className="caret"/>}`
   - Wrong: `<span className="caret animate-[blink_1s_steps(1)_infinite]"/>`
5. motion-durations MUST Take every duration from the motion tokens. Because reduced motion zeroes the tokens, and a typed duration keeps moving for people who asked it to stop.
   - Correct: `duration-(--dur-state)`
   - Wrong: `duration-[250ms]`
6. motion-name-properties NEVER Write transition-all; name the properties: colour, opacity, translate, clip-path. Because transition-all also tweens width and padding, so a hover shifts the layout around it.
   - Correct: `className="transition-[background-color]"`
   - Wrong: `className="transition-all"`
7. motion-loops NEVER Loop anything but the pending mark: no pulse, no glow, no light sweeping across, no scanlines. Because a loop pulls the eye from the one thing that changed, and the pending mark is the only sign work is running.
   - Correct: `<span className="pending"/>`
   - Wrong: `<div className="animate-pulse bg-well"/>`
8. motion-reduced MUST Let prefers-reduced-motion zero the wipes, draws, typing, scrambles and a button's light, so text, lines and colour are there at once; the pending mark stays still. Because moving text makes some people dizzy, and a still mark still says work is running.

## Tokens
| Token | Role | Use for | Not for | Light |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| `--dur-press` | a press: the colour step, no scale | a press | overlays | `80ms` |
| `--dur-state` | a state change: hover, an edge, a check | hover, an edge, a check; an overlay leaving | wipes | `120ms` |
| `--dur-overlay` | an overlay in; it leaves on --dur-state | an overlay arriving | hover | `160ms` |
| `--dur-wipe` | a region wiping in along its rule, start to end | a region or fill arriving along its rule | text | `240ms` |
| `--dur-draw` | a connector drawing out, one hop | tool-call connector, swimlane elbow |  | `300ms` |
| `--dur-type` | one character typing in, about 55 a second | typing | values being read | `18ms` |
| `--dur-scramble` | a mono label resolving from random glyphs, start to end | a label resolving | prose | `400ms` |
| `--dur-pending` | one cycle of the pending mark, four steps | button pending, tool call running |  | `800ms` |
| `--overlay-shift` | how far an anchored overlay travels in from its trigger | menu, popover, select, tooltip |  | `4px` |
| `--dur-light` | a button's fill and edge lightening under the pointer and settling back | a button's fill and edge lightening | a status change | `240ms` |
| `--dur-glow` | a button's light from below rising and fading, a beat behind its fill | a button's light from below | anything but slab and edged | `320ms` |
| `--ease-out` | the house curve: arrives fast and stops, no overshoot | every transition |  | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)` |
| `--ease-soft` | a softer arrival for light, no overshoot | primary button, secondary button hover |  | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.24, 1)` |
| `--ease-in` | an element leaving | overlay exit |  | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` |
| `--ease-linear` | wipes, typing and the pending steps | wipe, draw, type |  | `linear` |

## Decision table
| You need | Use |
|-|-|
| Press: the fill steps to its held colour and a button's light goes out; nothing scales | `--dur-press, --ease-out` |
| Light: a primary or secondary button's fill and edge lighten under the pointer and settle back after; its light from below follows on --dur-glow | `--dur-light, --ease-soft` |
| State: hover washes, a field's edge, a check; a state flip on a run (running to failed) is a cut | `--dur-state, --ease-out` |
| Overlay in: a menu, popover or tooltip fades in as it slides --overlay-shift from its trigger; a dialog only fades (overlay-motion) | `--dur-overlay, --ease-out` |
| Overlay out: it leaves the way it came, faster | `--dur-state, --ease-in` |
| Wipe: a region, a meter fill or a bar arrives along its rule from the start edge (wipe) | `--dur-wipe, --ease-linear` |
| Draw: a connector draws out from its node, one hop at a time, and ends in a square (draw) | `--dur-draw, --ease-out` |
| Type: a label or a headline types in a character at a time behind the caret, then the caret goes | `--dur-type, --ease-linear` |
| Scramble: a mono label resolves from random glyphs, start to end, once, when it first appears or its value changes | `--dur-scramble, --ease-linear` |
| Pending: one lit square steps along four, a loop | `--dur-pending, steps(4)` |

## Scale
80, 120 and 160ms for presses, states and overlays; 240 and 320ms for a button's fill and its light from below, on the softer --ease-soft; 240ms wipes, 300ms a connector hop; 18ms a typed character, 400ms a scramble; the pending mark 800ms a cycle in four steps. One curve out, a softer one for a button's light, one in, linear for wipes and typing. No springs, no scale.

## Reject list
- No springs, bounces, overshoot or press scale.
- No transition-all.
- No loops but the pending mark.
- No caret blinking at rest.
- No scroll reveals.

## Related
- [Elevation](/systems/sodium/foundations/elevation.md): No shadows: an overlay is the panel with a rule edge, set apart by its fill and, for a dialog, the scrim.

--- name: Typography system: sodium kind: foundation source: registry/sodium/tokens.css last-updated: 2026-10-26 human: https://design.how/systems/sodium/foundations/typography --- # Typography Mono capitals for the interface, Inter Display for headlines and prose, one weight. ## Rules 1. typography-roles MUST Set text with a type-* role; never a raw size, weight, line height or tracking. Because a role carries its size, line, case and tracking together, and a raw size sits off the lines beside it. - Correct: `

` - Wrong: `

` 2. typography-caps-through-roles MUST Set interface words (buttons, tabs, tags, table heads, axes) in a label role: type-label, type-label-sm, type-label-lg or type-micro. Write the words in sentence case in the source; the role sets the capitals. Because the role carries the mono face, the capitals and the opened tracking together, so a hand-set uppercase class gets the case without the tracking and crowds. - Correct: `Queued` - Wrong: `Queued` 3. typography-sans-for-sentences NEVER Set a headline, a sentence or a description in a label role; mono capitals are for words a person scans, not reads. Because a sentence in capitals reads slowly and shouts, and the sans is what makes the mono labels stand apart. - Correct: `

The backfill wrote 1,204 partitions.

` - Wrong: `

The backfill wrote 1,204 partitions.

` 4. typography-mono-roles MUST Set code, logs and values as written in type-code or type-code-sm; set mono inside a sentence of sans with mono or , at 0.85 of the text around it. Never font-mono on its own. Because Commit Mono is 22% wider than Inter Display a to z, so at the sans size an ID inside a sentence reads a size bigger than the words around it. - Correct: `

Job job_8f2a91 failed

` - Wrong: `

Job job_8f2a91 failed

` 5. typography-one-weight NEVER Set a weight above 400 in either face; make hierarchy with size, case and colour. Because both faces ship one cut, Regular, so a bold class makes the browser fake a bold that smears the strokes. - Correct: `

` - Wrong: `

Labels are mono capitals (button text and status words at their control's size, column heads and field and stat labels in type-label-sm); IDs, names, paths, counts, durations and sizes are mono as written (a region header's name and a value in type-code, header, footer or row meta in type-code-sm); prose is the sans (FrameDescription, type-body-sm). Because a reader learns three voices once and then knows what a word is before reading it: capitals name a place, mono as written is a thing to compare or copy, the sans is a thing to read. - Correct: `{run.pipeline} 1.2M` - Wrong: `{run.pipeline} 1.2M` 7. typography-figures SHOULD Set a number in a cell, a strip, a meter or a block in type-code like any value; keep type-figure for the one KPI a chart frame leads with.
